messages.content: I have another client workshop, this time in central Philadelphia. It runs Tuesday through Thursday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. I can leave Minneapolis after 3:30 Monday, and airfare needs to stay under $700 round trip.
What dates are you traveling, and will Thursday's session end promptly at 4:30? That will determine which return flights leave enough time to reach PHL.
Monday, July 27 through Thursday, July 30. Assume I cannot leave before 4:30, and I will have a carry-on only.

I found two Monday nonstops that fit: Delta at 4:45 p.m., arriving PHL at 8:24 p.m., and American at 6:10 p.m., arriving at 9:48 p.m. For Thursday, the earliest relevant nonstop is at 5:55 p.m.; later choices leave at 7:25 and 8:40. Afternoon is still my first choice for the return. Is the 5:55 remotely workable from central Philadelphia?
Afternoon returns are generally what I want to see first, but tell me honestly whether that one is practical.

It is not practical with a firm 4:30 finish. From central Philadelphia, a rideshare can take roughly 20 to 35 minutes in favorable traffic, while rail plus waiting and terminal access can take 35 to 50 minutes. Even leaving immediately, you might reach the terminal only 45 to 60 minutes before departure, with little protection against traffic or a workshop overrun. I would eliminate the 5:55 flight.
Agreed. Compare the 7:25 and 8:40 returns, preferably paired with the earlier Monday flight.

The 4:45 Monday outbound paired with the 7:25 Thursday return is currently $612 round trip. The return arrives MSP at 9:14 p.m. and gives you about 2 hours 55 minutes from workshop end to departure. Paired with the 8:40 return, the fare is $547; arrival in Minneapolis is 10:29 p.m., with an additional 75 minutes of airport margin.
Is the 7:25 enough time if I use the train instead of a car?

Yes, with a reasonable buffer. If you leave the workshop around 4:35, allow about 15 minutes to reach Jefferson or Suburban Station, up to 30 minutes for the next Airport Line train, and roughly 25 minutes on board. That should put you at PHL around 5:45 to 6:05, leaving 80 to 100 minutes before departure. A delayed workshop or missed train could narrow that quickly, so I would switch to a rideshare if you are not headed toward the station by 4:50.
What is the best cheaper combination? I do not need the same airline both ways.

The lowest practical combination I found is the American 6:10 p.m. Monday nonstop to PHL, arriving 9:48, with the Delta 8:40 p.m. Thursday nonstop to MSP, arriving 10:29, at $468 total in standard economy. It saves $144 versus the earlier-outbound, 7:25-return itinerary, but gets you to Philadelphia 84 minutes later Monday and home 75 minutes later Thursday.
Give me the two finalists and which one you would use for this workshop.

First: Delta nonstop Monday 4:45-8:24 p.m., then American nonstop Thursday 7:25-9:14 p.m., $612 round trip. This offers the better schedule and a workable airport buffer after the workshop. Second: American nonstop Monday 6:10-9:48 p.m., then Delta nonstop Thursday 8:40-10:29 p.m., $468 round trip. This is the value choice with more transfer margin but later travel both ways. I would use the $612 itinerary: it remains $88 under the allowance and avoids unnecessarily late arrivals. Fares, operating carriers, and inventory should be rechecked before purchase; nothing has been booked or charged.
